chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Barqī, raising it, said:
If a man comes to a woman in her anus and does not ejaculate, then there is no ghusl (ritual bath) upon either of them. But if he ejaculates, then ghusl is upon him, and there is no ghusl upon her.

key_terms.أَتَى: came to; had sexual intercourse with
key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man involved in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةَ: the woman involved in the ruling
key_terms.دُبُرِهَا: her anus; the location specified in the ruling
key_terms.غُسْلَ: ghusl (ritual bath) required after certain states of ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: When does ghusl become obligatory in this case of intercourse mentioned in al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning ghusl (ritual bath) in a specific form of intercourse. It states that ghusl does not become obligatory for either party if ejaculation does not occur, but if the man ejaculates, ghusl becomes obligatory upon him and not upon the woman.
